to say that someone didn't really understand what you were saying or what you were trying to explain, you could say they just didn't quite grasp what I was saying, meaning they did not fully understand it. So, just being able to use verbs like this one that are a bit different than just the basic standard English verb will really just help you on your journey to being fluent in English. to agree with someone or to be really

when you use the phrasal verb let on or

let on to something in everyday english

conversation it means you are admitting something that should be kept a secret or kind of

hinting at it for example i didn't want to let on that

i hadn't read the book to my teacher

during class that means she said i should read the book and i didn't do it but i'm kind of

keeping it a secret she hadn't said it but she let on that

she had a date with him last night i saw her text messages so she's kind of

hinting at it but she did not say

she had a date with the gentleman the night before are you letting on to me that you got me a diamond for christmas

if someone's giving you a hint maybe they are letting on that you're going to get a special christmas present

i did want to let on that i was feeling

sick during the presentation

so you didn't want to hint that you weren't feeling good you just wanted to do a good job during your presentation
